task: T2: bound the payload and make truncation impossible to miss, in scripts/ralph-log.sh. An artifact larger than a declared cap is sent truncated rather than dropped, because a large diff is exactly the one worth reading — but a truncated artifact must announce itself in a way a reader cannot overlook, so that a clipped diff can never be mistaken for the whole of what the executor changed. State the cap in one place and make it overridable by the environment variable `HARNESS_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES`, so an operator can raise it without editing the script; an unset or malformed value means the default, never zero, because a cap of zero would silently ship nothing at all. The announcement must be plain text a reader cannot miss, and must contain both the word `truncated` and the artifact's ORIGINAL size in bytes as a decimal number. The marker must survive the truncation: a note appended after the cap has already been reached is not a marker, it is more bytes that were cut. Include in the announcement how many bytes the artifact actually held, since "this was clipped" and "this was clipped at 4 MiB out of 41 MiB" are different facts and only the second one tells a reader whether to go looking for the original. Change no call site added in T1 and add no new kinds.
